name: LSH-512
workload: eBACS/SUPERCOP long-message hashing throughput (median of many runs, computed from 1536/4096/18208-byte message timings) on an amd64 test machine
claimed_speedup: ~1.6x faster than BLAKE2b (2.14 vs 3.36 cycles/byte) and ~5.3x faster than SHA3-512 (2.14 vs 11.25 cycles/byte) on long messages (derived from page data)
hardware: amd64-alder eBACS test machine: 2022 Intel Core i3-12100 (Golden Cove, model 90675-00), 4x3300MHz, supercop-20260831
tradeoffs: LSH uses a wider 128-byte block and a generalized-Feistel structure unrelated to Merkle-Damgard SHA-2 or sponge-based SHA-3/BLAKE2; far fewer independent implementations, audits, and years of cryptanalysis than SHA-2/SHA-3/BLAKE2. Only actively-maintained C/C++ library implementation found is Crypto++ (SSE2/AVX2 code, header cites Korea Internet & Security Agency spec).
caveats: The eBACS/SUPERCOP cycles-per-byte numbers are from SUPERCOP's own bundled LSH implementation (submitted by/derived from the KISA designers), not confirmed to be byte-identical to Crypto++'s AVX2 code, though Crypto++ is cited here as the actively-maintained, permissively-licensed C++ implementation of the same standardized algorithm (LSH-512, Korean standard KS X 3262, also ISO/IEC 10118-3:2018). Compiler and flags used per-implementation are not shown on the results page, so tier is capped at B rather than A. Academic cryptanalysis exists on step-reduced/free-start variants of LSH (e.g. IACR eprint 2015/494, later withdrawn); no practical break of full-round LSH-512 is known. Crypto++'s license is public-domain per its own License.txt (compilation copyright only), not a formal SPDX id; treat as no-patent-grant public domain.
found_via: bench.cr.yp.to eBACS/SUPERCOP hash benchmark results table for amd64-alder (Golden Cove), cross-checked via gh code search for LSH_256/LSH512 implementations

name: LSH-256
workload: eBACS/SUPERCOP long-message hashing throughput (median of many runs, computed from 1536/4096/18208-byte message timings) on an amd64 test machine
claimed_speedup: ~1.7x faster than BLAKE2s (3.13 vs 5.24 cycles/byte) and ~1.9x faster than SHA3-256 (3.13 vs 5.96 cycles/byte) on long messages (derived from page data)
hardware: amd64-alder eBACS test machine: 2022 Intel Core i3-12100 (Golden Cove, model 90675-00), 4x3300MHz, supercop-20260831
tradeoffs: LSH-256 is slower than plain SHA-256 (3.13 vs 2.05 cycles/byte on this machine) so it only beats BLAKE2s/SHA3-256, not the primary SHA-2 baseline; wider 128-byte block and generalized-Feistel structure differ from Merkle-Damgard/sponge designs; far less independent scrutiny/adoption outside Korea/ISO context.
caveats: Same SUPERCOP-vs-Crypto++ implementation caveat as the LSH-512 entry: eBACS benchmarks its own bundled LSH code, not confirmed identical to Crypto++'s AVX2 path. Compiler/flags per-implementation not shown on the results page, capping tier at B. Academic free-start/reduced-round cryptanalysis exists (IACR eprint 2015/494, withdrawn); full-round LSH-256 has no known practical break. Crypto++ license is public-domain per License.txt, no formal SPDX id, no patent grant.
